doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Memorable gigs
summary: His favorites: the Half Note with Al Cohn and Zoot Sims, Herb Alpert, Becky Kilgore in Portland, and the Algonquin.

bands.name: Al Cohn and Zoot Sims band

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. If you look back in your career — this is kind of a hard question — but are any gigs or certain times that stand out as really memorable, either negative or positive or humorous reasons?
Oh Jeez, well Monk, I mean there’s so—

It’s one gig after another, I mean what do you want? Each one of them, they all had their own stories. I guess the gig I think of the most as my golden age of New York playing was the one at the Half Note, which I held, along with other piano players, Ross Tompkins and Roger Kellaway and I maybe, were the three players that were used as house players. We were the utility guys. So we got to play with a lot of great players. And my specialty was with Al Cohn and Zoot Sims. That was the band I felt at home with. I spent eight years with them.
They were a great match, weren’t they?

Yeah. Oh yeah. And then in L.A., oh I don’t know I guess the most fun I had was the Herb Alpert days. In Portland I think my favorite gig was with Becky Kilgore, the singer, the Portland singer who I met up there and we had a job together in a hotel two nights a week for five years. And just a duo. And I loved that gig. And last week I finished three weeks at the Algonquin in New York in what I described to myself as the favorite gig of my life it was so much fun. So that was — I just finished a memorable gig.
Who was on that gig, was it just you?
It was just me at the Algonquin, yeah.
Yeah it was great, it was great.
